item.title: Pakistan's Opening Partnerships Struggle: A Historic Low Against England

item.content:encoded:
Pakistan's Opening Partnerships Struggle: A Historic Low Against England Pakistan's opening pair aggregates just 20 runs against England in the series. Using three different pairings, none succeeded in establishing a solid partnership. This poor run is the worst in 35 years. England dominated with a first innings lead, while Pakistan fared better in their second innings. Devdiscourse News Desk | Updated: 11-09-2026 19:53 IST | Created: 11-09-2026 19:53 IST

Azan Awais. (Photo: Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Pakistan's opening batsmen have experienced their worst collective performance in 35 years, amassing a mere 20 runs across the series against England. Saim Ayub and Azan Awais failed to construct notable partnerships at Edgbaston, marking Pakistan's third unsuccessful opener pairing in this challenging series. Previously, Azan Awais and Imam-ul-Haq took the crease in the first Test, followed by Shan Masood and Azan in the second. Unfortunately, none have managed to make an impact. In their initial effort, Azan and Imam left the scoreboard barren across two innings, while the Lord's Test saw Azan and Shan combine for only five and seven runs. At Edgbaston, Azan and Saim totaled eight and zero, respectively, bringing the series total to an uninspiring 20 runs—matching their lowest since a 1990/91 home series against the West Indies. As an opener, Azan Awais has accrued 129 runs from six innings at an average of 21.50, including just one half-century. His partners Imam (42 and 0), Shan (1 and 26), and Saim (0 and 0) have struggled to support him effectively. In their latest match, England elected to field first, promptly dismissing Pakistan for a scant 133, with Saud Shakeel (43) and Mohammad Abbas (21) the only notable contributors. England's bowlers Josh Tongue (4/42), Ollie Robinson (3/15), and Jofra Archer (3/25) proved too formidable for Pakistan. England capitalized robustly, posting a first innings total of 453, spurred by significant contributions from Emilio Gay (60), Harry Brook (75), Dan Lawrence (65), and Jamie Smith (69). Debutant Razaullah's valiant effort yielded a four-wicket haul for 148 runs. Pakistans response in the second innings was more promising, with Azan Awais scoring a vigorous 59 from 84 balls, joined by an unbeaten Shan Masood (83*) and Babar Azam (26*), as they reached 184/3 at lunch, trailing by 136 runs.

item.content:encoded:
US Inflation Pressures Intensify with August Price Hikes In August, US consumer prices saw a notable increase of 0.4%, driven largely by a rise in gasoline and energy costs. Over the past year, energy prices surged, contributing significantly to inflationary pressure, while core CPI also rose due to higher prices in sectors such as communication and transportation. Devdiscourse News Desk | Updated: 11-09-2026 18:39 IST | Created: 11-09-2026 18:39 IST

Representative image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Consumer prices in the United States experienced a marked rise of 0.4% in August, a significant increase from July's 0.1% jump, according to the latest statistics from the US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS). The surge was primarily driven by gasoline and energy prices. The Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) recorded a steady 3.4% increase over the 12 months ending in August, consistent with July's annual rise. Gasoline prices rose sharply by 3.9% this month, contributing to over a third of the overall index's monthly increment. While the broader energy index increased by 2.1% in August, shelter costs saw a modest 0.3% rise. Core CPI, excluding volatile food and energy prices, rose by 0.3% in August. The notable sectors contributing to this increase included communication, lodging, airline fares, and used cars. Despite general upward pressure, medical care prices fell by 0.2%, while motor vehicle insurance dropped by 0.8%. On an annual scale, energy remained a significant contributor to inflation, while notable price hikes were seen in the transportation sector.

(With inputs from agencies.)

This move, part of a larger escalation backed by Iran, could reshape dynamics in the Middle East conflict, potentially impacting global oil prices and Saudi Arabia's crude exports. Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi forces have taken control of the strategic island of Perim in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a critical global shipping route, intensifying the ongoing Middle East conflict, according to Yemeni government sources cited by Reuters. This development follows the withdrawal of Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces from Perim and the mainland Red Sea coastal town of Dhubab. The Houthis' strategic positioning could provide Iran with a significant advantage over the U.S., potentially affecting oil prices and geopolitical dynamics. Satellite imagery has shown smoke near Saudi Arabia's vital East-West oil pipeline, further raising tensions. While Saudi Arabia has not confirmed this incident, the conflict's escalation has already impacted oil supply and heightened regional instability.
